report:
**Conclusion**
No, high-quality clinical evidence demonstrates that ivermectin does **not** lower the risk of death in COVID-19 patients.

Rigorous evaluations by major medical bodies and systematic reviews consistently show no mortality benefit:

1. **Cochrane Systematic Review**: Comprehensive meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) found high-certainty evidence that ivermectin does not reduce all-cause mortality, prevent clinical deterioration, or improve symptom resolution compared to standard care or placebo.
2. **World Health Organization (WHO)**: The WHO Therapeutics and COVID-19 Guidelines recommend against using ivermectin to treat COVID-19 outside of controlled clinical trials, concluding that available evidence shows no meaningful reduction in mortality or hospitalization.
3. **National Institutes of Health (NIH)**: The NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines Panel explicitly recommends against using ivermectin for COVID-19. Large, well-designed clinical trials (including the TOGETHER, ACTIV-6, and PRINCIPLE trials) demonstrated no statistically significant reduction in risk of death or disease progression.

Overall, scientific consensus confirms that ivermectin is ineffective at reducing mortality from COVID-19.

**Sources:**
* Cochrane Review: https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD015017.pub3/abstract
* World Health Organization: https://www.who.int/news-room/feature-stories/detail/who-advises-that-ivermectin-only-be-used-to-treat-covid-19-within-clinical-trials
* NIH Treatment Guidelines: https://www.covid19treatmentguidelines.nih.gov/therapies/miscellaneous-drugs/ivermectin/
